system.summary: Selected words in an English letter (names, places, key words) written as runs of two-digit numbers, one number per letter: a shifted alphabet over 60-85 (A=77 ... I=85, J=60 ... Z=76). The writer often writes only the first letters and the last letter of a word, with a dash.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct pairs that occur (measured, 19 including the doubtful 7?7); the alphabet has 26. key_order alphabetical = the numbers run in alphabet order from A=77, wrapping 85 to 60. Separation: digits mostly run together, with spaces, commas, dots and dashes in places.

solution.what: PDF GET from the sandbox refused (HTML 3,038 B); both images read in the JSTOR viewer via Claude in Chrome, screen zooms.
Prior art: Cyphersolver issues/PRs/catalogue/leads, DECODE live search, JSTOR item and Fenian code-word list, web; books not reachable (PRIOR_ART.md).
Whole letter transcribed; 13 number groups, 71 two-digit pairs, all in 60-85 but one doubtful; 5 doubts listed; frozen and stamped 23:31:52Z. Key hypothesis formed before the freeze (disclosed).
G08 '85 68 85 69 84 / 73 65 68 62 80' after 'we had the whole ... with us': x-y-x pattern read as IRI-; IRISH WORLD fits all 10 pairs under one shift, A=77.
Decoder v1 applied the frozen key; crashed on the doubtful token 7?7 (bug).

Decoder v2 (doubt handling fixed, key unchanged), one pass over all 13 groups: RUS-A, DEC x4, WOLFETONE, SEC[r]ET OR--, IRISH WORLD, R--S, PAT--S, AUTNONMY, OUR NAT-E L-D, C?NADA. Pairs 67/71 = 94.4%; groups with identified meaning 8/13 = 61.5% (under the 65% line: fails at group level).

5 fixed test words against the English lexicon: real key 5/5; other 25 shifts 0; 5,000 random keys 0 >= real at seeds 20261112 and 7 (max 2); 5,000 ciphertext shuffles under the real key 0 >= real at both seeds (max 2). No held-out test possible.

Blind second reading of the number runs by an isolated AI reader from the crops only, frozen and stamped 23:37:20Z: 70/71 pairs agree (G13 pair 2 differs, both doubtful); extra pair 64 at the end of G07 (OR--N?).
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 70 tokens, 18 types, en-modern order 4: reading -3.559 per letter; Verdict: too short.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -3.559; polyphony 0.0; 1 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached n/a

outcome.method_basis: Key recovered from the ciphertext with the crib IRISH WORLD (pattern x-y-x), one parameter for all 26 values; checked on WOLFE TONE, CANADA, RUS-A, PAT--S, OUR NAT-E L-D, which were not used to build it. Figures of record (first pass, measured): pairs 67/71 = 94.4%; groups with an identified meaning 8/13 = 61.5%, UNDER the project's own 65% line, failed at group level (G02-G05 DEC, one unidentified person, and G09 R--S). G11 emended (AUTNONMY written, AUTONOMY read; 3 pairs). G13 pair 2 doubtful. Exposure: the first transcriber saw the key pattern before the freeze. Blind AI second reading 70/71 = 98.59% of pairs agree, with an extra 64 at the end of G07. Controls: 0/5,000 random keys and 0/5,000 shuffled ciphertexts at seeds 20261112 and 7; other 25 shifts 0. fraction_read = clean pairs / pairs = 67/71. No person has checked it.

texts.summary: The writer reports from London that his mission succeeded: with 'the Infant' he met a man written DEC, put the advantages to Russia of an understanding, said the whole Irish World was with them, and was asked whether a diversion in Canada was feasible. The letter breaks off.

reading_review.note: Read the whole decoded letter as sentences (emailed reading, 26 Nov 2026) and graded it A. His notes: Russia and Canada confirmed; DEC (80 81 79) is the same person in all four places, the dots and dashes between the numbers being loose handwriting; R--s read as 'revolutionaries' (sense, not code: only R and S are written); 'autonomy of our native land'. DEC not identified. A person read the reading; he did not re-check the transcription digit by digit against the images.
